questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He's been __working late into the night__, trying to finish his thesis before the deadline.

options.text: burning the candle at both the ends

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"burning the midnight oil"** means working late into the night or staying up late to complete tasks. (रात भर काम करना)

 
 
• **Example:** She was burning the midnight oil to prepare for her exams.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase "working late into the night" can be appropriately substituted with the idiom "burning the midnight oil".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Burning the ships** (जहाज जलाना): Refers to taking an irreversible step that eliminates the possibility of retreat.

 
 
• **Example:** By quitting his job, he was burning the ships to start his own business.
 
 
 
• **Burning bridges** (पुल जलाना): Refers to destroying relationships or connections that could be useful in the future.
 
 
• **Example:** He regretted burning bridges with his old colleagues after he needed their help.
 
 
 
• **Burning the candle at both ends** (दोनों छोर से मोमबत्ती जलाना): Refers to overworking oneself by staying up late and waking up early, often leading to exhaustion.
 
 
• **Example:** She has been burning the candle at both ends to manage her job and studies.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Fall between two stools

options.text: Fail to achieve either of two aims
Confused to select either of two options

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Fail to achieve either of two aims.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Fall between two stools"** means to fail to achieve either of two aims or objectives, often due to indecision or poor planning. (दो लक्ष्यों में से किसी को प्राप्त करने में विफल होना)

 
 
• **Example:** He tried to please both his boss and his colleagues, but he fell between two stools and ended up disappointing both.
 
 
 
• **Fail to achieve either of two aims** signifies that efforts or decisions made to achieve two different goals resulted in failure for both. (दो उद्देश्यों में से किसी को हासिल करने में विफलता)
 
 
• **Example:** The product launch aimed to appeal to both teenagers and adults, but it fell between two stools and failed to attract either group.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Fall upon the hurdles continuously** (लगातार बाधाओं पर गिरना): This refers to repeatedly encountering obstacles or difficulties, but it is not relevant to the given idiom.

 
 
• **Example:** The athlete fell upon the hurdles continuously during the race.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Succeed to achieve both aims** (दोनों लक्ष्यों को प्राप्त करने में सफल होना): This refers to successfully achieving two objectives, which is opposite to the idiom's meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** She succeeded in achieving both her academic and extracurricular goals.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Confused to select either of two options** (दो विकल्पों में से किसी एक को चुनने में उलझन): This refers to a state of confusion in decision-making, but it does not align with the idiom's meaning.

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with an adverbial usage error.

David loudly / opened the gift / presented by / his sister.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adverb "**loudly**" is incorrectly used in the sentence as it describes how David opened the gift.
 
• However, "**opened**" is a physical action and using "**loudly**" to modify it is semantically odd unless there's a context where the action of opening itself produced a loud noise, which is uncommon and unintended here.
 
• A more appropriate placement would be an adverb describing **emotion** (e.g., *excitedly*) or **manner** (e.g., *carefully*, *quickly*), rather than **volume**.
 
• Hence, the adverbial usage in **“David loudly”** is inappropriate in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"David **excitedly**__ opened the gift presented by his sister."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Opened the gift** is a verb phrase correctly placed without error.
 
• **Presented by** and **his sister** form a correct passive structure indicating the doer.
